intro.title: Pick Your Vehicle
intro.text: You want the White House and have not yet chosen which party to ride there. Nine questions on the issues that split the country. Each runs from one lunatic fringe to the other, with two tamer answers in between. Answer what you actually believe: one primary will crown you for it and the other will eat you alive, and you should know which is which before you file.

questions.context: Roe v. Wade was overturned in June 2022, and each state now sets its own abortion law.
questions.prompt: Donor dinner, first course. The woman with the biggest checkbook asks what the abortion law should be. She can smell a dodge. Your answer?

options.label: Abortion at any point, for any reason, free. A drive-through if demand allows
Legal in most cases, with some limits late in pregnancy
Illegal in most cases, except rape, incest or to save the mother
Total ban from conception, no exceptions at all. The doctor gets a cell

questions.prompt: Debate prep, 2 a.m. Your consultant says the gun answer costs you votes either way, so give the one you mean. What do you do about guns?

options.label: Repeal the Second Amendment, seize every gun, melt them into park benches
Owning guns is fine. A background check on every sale, no exceptions
No new gun laws. Enforce the ones already on the books
Any weapon, anyone, anywhere, no checks, no permits. Tanks ship free

questions.prompt: One rival calls you soft, another calls you cruel. Millions of immigrants live here illegally. What do you do with them?

options.label: Open borders, abolish ICE, citizenship at the door. The wall becomes a ramp
Legal status for those who work and obey the law, plus a secure border
Secure the border first, then deport the ones who commit crimes
Deport everyone here illegally and whoever hid them. Weld the border shut

questions.prompt: An insurance lobbyist waits in your outer office with a check and a smile. Before he comes in: how should Americans get health insurance?

options.label: Outlaw private insurance tomorrow. One government plan, and insurers on welfare
Keep private insurance and add a government plan anyone can choose
Keep private insurance and force the insurers to compete on price
Abolish Medicare and Medicaid. The market decides who lives. Tip your surgeon

questions.prompt: Your finance chair wants the tax plan on one index card before he makes a single call. Which way do taxes and government spending go?

options.label: Tax billionaires out of existence. Seize the yachts and house people on them
The rich pay somewhat more, and the programs we have stay safe
Hold taxes where they are and slow the growth of spending
Abolish the income tax and the IRS. Fund the army with a bake sale

questions.prompt: An oil executive and a climate billionaire both want breakfast with you. Only one leaves happy. What does your energy policy put first?

options.label: Ban oil, gas and coal outright, today. Winter will be a learning experience
A steady shift to clean energy, bought with incentives, not bans
Every energy source, oil and gas included, and prices kept low
Drill everywhere, national parks included. Scrap the EPA. The climate can sue

questions.prompt: Crime leads every newscast in the state you cannot lose. The cameras are outside and your rivals have spoken. How do you make people safer?

options.label: Abolish the police and empty the prisons. Burglars get a social worker
Keep the police funded, and punish officers who abuse the badge
Hire more police officers and stand behind them
Soldiers on every street, life sentences for everything. Lose the key

questions.prompt: The moderator saves the one that makes candidates sweat. Gender transition, children, sports and medicine: what are your rules?

options.label: Raise all children gender-neutral until they can say their gender. Beige, by law
Leave it to families, doctors and local sports bodies, not politicians
Sports by biological sex, and no medical transition before 18
Ban gender transition outright, at any age, adults included. Your body, my call

questions.context: In June 2023 the Supreme Court ended the use of race in college admissions.
questions.prompt: A college president and a CEO corner you at a fundraiser. Both are donors. What do you do about race, diversity and DEI?

options.label: Reparations now, and racial quotas for every college, board and bowling team
Back diversity programs and outreach, but no racial preferences
No racial preferences anywhere. Merit alone decides
Ban DEI, shut every diversity office, repeal the Civil Rights Act for dessert

tiebreak.prompt: A dead heat. You have managed to betray both parties equally. One question settles it. Which frightens you more?

options.label: A government that does too little and leaves people to sink
A government that does too much and gets in everyone's way

dem.strong: Your answers clearly place you in the Democratic primary. On nearly every issue you stand where its loudest voters stand, so they will trust you, and trust is the easiest thing in politics to spend.
dem.lean: On balance, your answers place you in the Democratic primary. You broke with its voters more than once, and your rivals have already written those answers down.
dem.barely: A near call: you could have sold yourself to either side. Your answers place you, narrowly, in the Democratic primary, where half the room will suspect you are a plant.

gop.strong: Your answers clearly place you in the Republican primary. On nearly every issue you stand where its loudest voters stand, so they will trust you, and trust is the easiest thing in politics to spend.
gop.lean: On balance, your answers place you in the Republican primary. You broke with its voters more than once, and your rivals have already written those answers down.
gop.barely: A near call: you could have sold yourself to either side. Your answers place you, narrowly, in the Republican primary, where half the room will suspect you are a plant.
